historical_aborted_g2r_relocation.source_lock_schema_note: This schema records locked sources, existing CKL source references, and withheld boundaries. It has no unresolved/conflicted source disposition counters; validation outcomes are reported in g2-validation-report.json.

purpose: G2R2 source ownership and direct-passage applicability lock for the isolated Genesis 6-9 context object.

source_policy.copyright_boundary: Paraphrase claims and retain locators; do not copy commentary prose.
source_policy.historical_source_reuse: No historical source ID is reused directly. Thirteen distinct object-local aliases preserve bibliographic facts while leaving canonical historical ownership unchanged.
source_policy.local_alias_pattern: g2r2-local-<historical-source-id>; same bibliographic identity/locator/URL, explicitly documented as the same publication/work.
source_policy.schema_limitation: CanonicalEvidenceItem has no general non_applicability field. Non-applicability is stated in notes/source records; schema cannot machine-type those contextual relationships.
source_policy.scripture_reference_rule: Only passages that should receive each evidence item may appear as scripture_references. Comparative texts and later reception are source/prose context only.

sources.author: Jaap J. T. Doedens
sources.locator: Interpretive history and analysis of Genesis 6:1–4
sources.notes: Monograph surveying the text, ancient context, and reception of the principal interpretive positions; used to preserve disagreement rather than select one view.
sources.title: The Sons of God in Genesis 6:1–4: Analysis and History of Exegesis

sources.author: Ancient Jewish text
sources.notes: Second Temple reception witness. Its angelic interpretation is later reception of Genesis and is not evidence for Genesis 6's immediate wording.
sources.title: 1 Enoch 6–16

sources.author: Ancient Jewish text
sources.notes: Second Temple reception witness. Angelic descent and offspring traditions are recorded as reception, not imported into Genesis 6's own claims.
sources.title: Book of Jubilees 5:1–11

sources.author: Kenneth C. Way
sources.locator: Discussion of Genesis 6:3 and the 120-year lifespan/countdown readings
sources.notes: Recent scholarly discussion records both major readings; the item marks the verse as disputed.
sources.title: Goodness and Creaturely Finitude: Time and Limits in Genesis 1–11 and in Christian Practice

sources.author: Sarah Schwartz
sources.locator: Article discussion of Genesis 6:9 and the Noah toledot section
sources.notes: Literary study of the toledot formula and the narrative function of Noah's genealogy heading.
sources.title: Narrative Toledot Formulae in Genesis: The Case of Heaven and Earth, Noah, and Isaac

sources.author: NET Bible Translators
sources.locator: Genesis 8:4, note 1: Ararat/Urartu region and the plural mountain phrase
sources.notes: Identifies Ararat with the mountainous Urartu region north of Mesopotamia; the note does not identify a particular modern peak or ark site.
sources.title: NET Bible Notes on Genesis 8:4

sources.author: Petrus J. van Dyk
sources.locator: Discussion of ruach in Genesis 1:2 and 8:1; DOI 10.4102/hts.v73i3.4670
sources.notes: Argues for connected wind/breath/spirit senses and a possible creation/re-creation resonance. The CKL item retains wind as the immediate sense and records resonance as a proposal, not a settled lexical result.
sources.publisher: HTS Teologiese Studies/Theological Studies 73, no. 3, article 4670
sources.title: The Spirit of God, or is it?

sources.author: Shalom E. Holtz
sources.locator: Discussion of the pitch term *kofer* in Genesis 6:14 and its Akkadian comparative context
sources.notes: Supports the pitch/Akkadian comparison only; the uncertain *gopher* wood term is not attributed to this article, and no archaeological ark identification is asserted.
sources.title: The Flood Story in Its Ancient Near Eastern Context

sources.author: Tremper Longman III and John H. Walton
sources.locator: Their literary and theological argument concerning flood scope and ancient rhetorical conventions
sources.notes: A documented regional/hyperbolic reading of the narrative's universal language, included as one interpretation rather than a geological finding or consensus verdict.
sources.title: The Lost World of the Flood: Mythology, Theology, and the Deluge Debate

sources.author: Guy Darshan
sources.locator: Comparative analysis of raven and dove episodes in Genesis 8 and ancient flood narratives
sources.notes: Comparison supports literary context; ancient comparanda are kept out of Scripture applicability anchors.
sources.title: The Motif of Releasing Birds in Ancient Near Eastern Flood Stories

sources.author: Shlomo Zuckier
sources.locator: Discussion of reah nihoah and Genesis 8:20–22
sources.notes: Surveys readings of pleasing aroma language and cautions against assuming that the text depicts divine need for food.
sources.publisher: Journal for the Study of the Old Testament
sources.title: Nothing to Sniff At: Odorless Reah Nihoah in Early Biblical Interpretation

sources.author: Robert Gnuse
sources.locator: Discussion of Genesis 9:1–17, beneficiaries, food permission, and covenant scope
sources.notes: Supports a passage-bounded account of human and animal beneficiaries and the covenant's scope.
sources.title: The Covenant with Noah in Genesis 9

sources.author: Ruhama Bonfil and Robert Bonfil
sources.locator: Chapter on Genesis 9:12–17 and ancient bow/rainbow symbolism
sources.notes: Presents a weapon-in-cloud proposal as a possible symbolic reading; the lexical observation and the proposal remain distinct.
sources.title: I Have Set My Bow in the Cloud: Symbolism and Myth

sources.author: Brian Rainey
sources.notes: Argues for social shame and exposure as a key interpretive frame; it is one proposal among debated readings.
sources.title: Indecent Exposure: Social Shame, ʿerwâ and Interpretation of Genesis 9:20–27

sources.author: Matthew R. Schlimm
sources.locator: Article discussion of Noah's inebriation, speech, and interpretations of Genesis 9:20–27
sources.notes: Treats the narrative's moral and reception questions without making a later racialized reading part of the text.
sources.title: Noah's Inebriated Curse (Genesis 9:20–27)

sources.author: T. Desmond Alexander
sources.locator: Pages 27–58; alternative reading of the identity of the youngest son in Genesis 9:24
sources.notes: A minority proposal that Canaan, rather than Ham, may be the son implicated by the narrative; recorded as a proposal, not a settled reading.
sources.title: Exonerating Ham: An Alternative Reading of Genesis 9:20–27

withheld: No specific modern Mount Ararat peak or ark site.
No geological adjudication of flood extent.
